summary.text: Saint Flavian was Patriarch of Constantinople and an opponent of Eutyches. He suffered violence at the Ephesus assembly of 449 and died soon afterward.

blocks.text: Before becoming patriarch he was a priest and caretaker of church vessels in Constantinople’s cathedral. He succeeded Patriarch Proclus during a period of conflict over how to confess Christ’s divinity and humanity.
blocks.locator: Opening paragraphs on presbyteral service and succession

blocks.text: In 448 he convened a local council to examine Eutyches’ teaching. The next year a council at Ephesus reinstated Eutyches and condemned Saint Flavian through intimidation and force. Orthodox sources call this assembly the Robber Council, distinguishing it from an Ecumenical Council.
blocks.reason: Necessary concise source-bound biography and identity clarification. The modern ecclesiastical source is summarized rather than substantially reproduced; traditional narratives remain explicitly attributed.

blocks.text: The OCA describes severe beatings, imprisonment in chains, and a sentence of banishment before his death in August 449. It honors him with the title Confessor. His death followed the persecution described in the account.

blocks.text: His opposition to Eutyches forms part of the conflict preceding Chalcedon. Saint Pulcheria later arranged the return of his relics to Constantinople. His commemoration preserves the distinction between an assembly’s political power and its reception by the Church.
